about.title: Victorville Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Victorville is home to roughly 122,225 people, and its clinics and emergency departments serve a wide stretch of the High Desert well beyond the city line. In 2025 alone, public records show 753 people were injured in 522 collisions here, many along Bear Valley Road, Amargosa Road, Mojave Drive and Route 395, and a large share of them passed through local emergency care. Most of that care is good. Some of it is not. A missed fracture on an X-ray, a medication given at the wrong dose, a surgical step skipped, a warning sign in a lab result that no one acted on: these are the kinds of errors that can turn a recoverable injury into a lasting one. Under California's MICRA law, medical malpractice claims follow their own rules. You generally have one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. A 90-day notice must go to the provider before a lawsuit is filed. And a qualified medical expert nearly always has to confirm that the care fell below the accepted standard, because a bad outcome by itself is not malpractice. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Victorville residents with an independent attorney who can review the records and explain, honestly, whether there is a case.

whyChoose.title: Why Victorville Residents Use LawProactive for Malpractice Questions

items.title: MICRA's clock is short and specific
items.desc: California generally gives one year from discovery and no more than three from the injury, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice before filing. The attorneys we connect you with know these deadlines and can tell you quickly whether time is still on your side.

items.title: Expert review, not guesswork
items.desc: Nearly every California malpractice case needs a qualified medical expert to say the care fell below the standard. Attorneys in our network have the relationships to get records reviewed by the right specialist before anyone commits to a claim.

items.title: Current numbers on the non-economic cap
items.desc: MICRA caps non-economic damages, and that cap rises every year. An attorney who works these cases in San Bernardino County can explain the figure that applies to your situation rather than an outdated one, and works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was treated at a Victorville emergency room after a crash on Bear Valley Road and they missed a broken bone. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but the missed injury alone doesn't settle the question. A qualified medical expert would need to look at the imaging and the notes and determine whether a reasonably careful provider would have caught it under the same circumstances. If the delay made your injury worse, that matters too. An attorney can request the records and get that review started at no cost to you.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and in no case more than three years from when the injury happened. There are limited exceptions, such as for minors or when a foreign object was left in the body. You also have to send the provider a 90-day notice before filing suit, which is one reason it helps to speak with an attorney early rather than close to the deadline.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything, and are you a law firm?
items.answer: No and no. LawProactive is a free connection service; we are not a law firm and do not give legal advice ourselves. We match you with an independent attorney who handles medical malpractice cases in the Victorville area. Those attorneys work on contingency, meaning they are paid only if there is a recovery.
